config.documentTitleFull: PETITION FOR EXPUNCTION OF AN ARREST RECORD WHERE THE COURT HAS NO HISTORY OF THE ARREST, PURSUANT TO T.C.A. § 40-32-109
config.courtCaption: IN THE [COURT HAVING JURISDICTION IN THIS MATTER — CRIMINAL, CIRCUIT OR GENERAL SESSIONS COURT; CONFIRM FROM YOUR OWN RECORD] OF [COUNTY — CONFIRM FROM YOUR OWN RECORD] COUNTY, STATE OF TENNESSEE

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: A person whose arrest record exists, but for whom the court with jurisdiction over the offence for which the person was arrested has no history of the arrest within the court's records, may petition that court. The subsection uses the permissive 'may petition'. Upon filing, the clerk serves the petition on the district attorney general for that judicial district.
Both the petitioner and the district attorney general may file evidence with the court.
The clerk's office searches the court's records and certifies to the court whether there is any history of the arrest.
The court reviews the clerk's certification and all evidence and may enter the order if it finds there is no history of the arrest within the court's record.
A person petitioning under the section must be charged the appropriate clerk's fee.

Applies the chapter's restoration effect: the petitioner is entitled to have all public records destroyed, is restored in contemplation of law to the status occupied before the arrest, must not suffer adverse effects or collateral disabilities by virtue of the offence, and is not guilty of perjury for failing to acknowledge the arrest in response to any inquiry.
Expressly exempts the court from submitting a certificate where the relief is granted pursuant to this section.

counselFlags: Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it.

No official Tennessee participant form exists. Both state form indices were inspected directly and neither publishes an expunction form of any kind; this is a negative finding established from the authoritative index, not a failure to search. A controlled custom instrument is therefore the only available strategy, and it is not represented as an official form.

Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025 and codified by Public Chapter 608 effective 2026-03-25, and clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering — the state's own expunction page still reasons from a section that has been nothing but definitions since 2025-04-24. A petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet carries the current citation and instructs the participant to confirm it with the clerk or the district attorney general before filing.
Tennessee expunction reaches no federal, military, tribal or out-of-state record, and a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on a clearance check.

The governing section prescribes no caption form and no contents for the participant's instrument. The caption follows the ordinary criminal-case style of the court having jurisdiction, with the filer designated as the source designates them. What individual clerks and courts in fact expect is not established and no county practice was surveyed; the caption is a visual- and counsel-review item.

This is the only Tennessee route in the chapter on which the participant writes the operative statutory petition. The section contains no cross-reference to the procedure section, so the duty on the office of the district attorney general to prepare the petition and proposed order does not reach it.
It also carries no waiting period, no 61-day pre-order clock, no rebuttable presumption and no two-year refiling bar; all of those live in the procedure section alone and none is imported here.

This route is not free and there is no waiver. The section makes the clerk's fee mandatory and contains no indigency, waiver or without-cost provision, in express contrast to the free non-conviction route. The amount is set by a separate fee statute whose current text was not retrievable from an official source, so no figure is quoted. The participant must be told this route is not free before anything is prepared.
No certificate step from the state bureau arises on this route; the court is expressly exempted, and it reviews only the clerk's certification and the evidence submitted.
Whether a prior court action or court file ever existed is not adjudicated here. The clerk searches and certifies and the court finds. A disputed history is handed off to an attorney.

The section prescribes no contents for the petition, so this instrument is drafted to the eligibility condition and to the finding the court must make. What individual clerks and courts in fact expect is not established and no county practice was surveyed.

The enacted text says the clerk certifies whether there is any history within the court's 'records' while the next subsection directs the court to find there is no history within the court's 'record'. The variance is in the enacted text and no erratum was located. It is reported without conclusion and this pleading does not lean on the distinction.

A participant whose case did reach the court and was dismissed, no-true-billed, nolle prossed or acquitted belongs on the free non-conviction route instead and is redirected there rather than paying here.

The state control number is a manual-completion item read from the participant's own criminal history. It stays a bracket in generated output; the order cannot be completed without it, and the participant is told to capture it early.

The shared renderer's fixed section heading "VI. VERIFICATION" is a Pennsylvania-derived artefact of the frozen renderer contract, not a Tennessee drafting choice. Nothing in the governing section requires verification. This is a visual- and counsel-review item.
No fee figure is quoted anywhere in this packet. The source records no retrievable amount, and the filing-fee field is left null rather than filled with a circulating number.
No fee-waiver instrument is included and the fee-waiver field is left null, because the source establishes no waiver mechanism for this route.
The governing section states no waiting period. None is pleaded, none is imported from a neighbouring section, and the waiting-period field is left null.

Notarization is not prescribed by the governing section and no verification statute exists to cite, so verificationStatute.citation is left null and the signature block carries no penalty citation. County practice may differ, and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk.

Self-help stop conditions: The court does in fact have a record of the arrest. That takes the participant out of this route entirely and into the § 40-32-106 analysis, which is the free route; the participant is redirected there rather than handed off. The district attorney general files evidence that the court does have a history of the arrest. That converts the matter into a contested question of fact and the participant is handed off to an attorney. Whether a prior court action or court file ever existed is disputed. LegalEase does not adjudicate that question: the clerk searches and certifies and the court finds, so a disputed history is handed off to an attorney. The participant cannot establish from the TBI criminal history that an arrest record exists at all. The participant is directed back to the TBI before the route reopens. The participant is seeking relief for a case that reached the court and was dismissed, no-true-billed, nolle prossed or acquitted. That is the free § 40-32-106 route and the participant is redirected to it rather than paying here. Federal, military, tribal or out-of-state records, immigration consequences and any security-clearance question, each of which is referred out because Tennessee expunction does not reach them.
